Meet Braino. He lives in your Mac's notch, and does what you say in the apps you already use.
WORKS IN WHAT YOU ALREADY USE
Someone to talk to, who actually gets it done.
Braino is a companion who lives in your Mac's notch. He knows your day and your people, and when you ask, he does the work in the apps you already use.
Tell him what you want and he does it, in the apps you already use, and remembers you. Nothing is sent, bought or posted without your yes.
Stop typing the same replies. Say “tell Priya Friday works.” He opens WhatsApp, writes it the way you would, and sends it after your yes.
Stop taking notes in meetings. He listens to the call or the lecture. Close the laptop and the notes are waiting: what was decided, and who does what.
Stop checking five apps every morning. Ask “what's today?” and get one answer: your meetings, your deadlines, and who is waiting on you.
Stop digging for that file. Say what it was about, and he finds it and opens it. No folders, no search bar.
Stop filling the same forms. Your name, your email, the login you always forget. He fills it in and stops before submit.
ONLY BRAINO Stop explaining yourself to your software. He remembers your people and what you told him last month, so you never start from zero.

We grew up watching Tony Stark talk to Jarvis and Jarvis just get it done. That is the future of computing we believe in, and now it is on the Mac you already own. Say it once, and Braino does it for you.
Clear your inbox Reads the thread, writes the reply in your voice, waits for your yes.
Plan your day Your classes, what is due and who is waiting, in one answer.
Send the file Finds the file you mean and sends it to the right person.

He runs on AffectiveOS, the layer we built for the Mac you already own.

AffectiveOS gives your Mac eyes to see your screen, ears to hear you, a voice to answer, hands to do the work, and a memory of you. It runs on top of macOS, so there is nothing to replace or reinstall.

/affectiveos.title: Introducing AffectiveOS · Affective
/affectiveos.pageDescription: Meet Braino. He lives in your Mac's notch and does what you say in the apps you already use. Made by Affective, running on AffectiveOS.
blocks: Introducing AffectiveOS, an agentic, voice-first operating system that lets you talk to your Mac and have it do the work. It sees your screen, hears you, answers out loud, acts in your apps, and remembers you.
Figure 1. You speak; your words appear; the steps run, and it stops before anything is posted.

Here is the thing that bugged us. Computers got faster every year, and we still spend the day operating them: open this, find that, copy, paste, click, send. We were learning the computer's language, the way we always have. Commands, then menus, then taps.

We think the next step is the one where the computer learns ours. You say what you want, the way you would say it to a friend, and it happens. That is AffectiveOS. And Braino, a companion who lives in your notch, is the first thing we built on it.
We grew up watching Tony Stark talk to Jarvis. This is our way of building it, for the Mac you already own.
So what does it actually give your Mac? Five things it never had.
Senses. It sees the screen you are on and hears you, even for an hour straight. Nothing to copy, paste or explain.
Voice. It talks back, out loud. Cut it off mid-sentence and it stops, like a person would.
Hands. Say the task and it gets done in the apps you already use: the message sent, the file found, the form filled. 129 tools, on the real Mac.
Memory. Everything it hears, says and does lands here and stays, on your Mac. Not what you typed into a chat: what actually happened, all day.
Trust. Anything that spends money, sends a message, posts in public or deletes something waits for your yes.

One brain, two speeds. Think of how you work. Some things you just do without thinking, and some you stop and plan. AffectiveOS is the same. A reflex on your Mac figures out what you mean: a chat, a quick action or a bigger job. The easy ones it just does. The big ones go to the thinking, which plans the whole job once. And the reflex learns from the thinking, so what needed a plan yesterday can be a reflex tomorrow.

We buy the thinking, build the hands, and keep the memory. We are not trying to train the biggest model. We use the best ones of the day, from labs like Anthropic and OpenAI, and swap them as they get better. Everything that acts on your Mac, we built. And what it remembers is yours, on your machine.
An illustration, not a measurement: the steps you take by hand for everyday jobs, against saying one sentence.
Figure 2. What each kind of tool covers today.

Honestly, every tool out there does one piece of this well. A chat assistant is smart, but then you do the work. Dictation types faster, and that is it. Cloud agents can act, but on some computer that is not yours. We wanted all of it together, on the Mac you already own.
A general comparison of categories, not of any one product. Categories change quickly; this reflects them as of September 2026.
Figure 3. One request, broken down. Typical, not a benchmark: the hands take as long as the job does.

Most of what we ask for is small, and small things should feel instant. So a reflex on the Mac handles them itself, in about five hundredths of a second, before any big model is even involved. Bigger jobs get planned once, in about two seconds, and then you watch them happen.
Typical times measured in our private beta on a MacBook, from the moment you finish speaking. They vary with the job, the network and the model in use.

Something that sees your screen all day has to earn that. So what AffectiveOS remembers stays on your Mac. Private windows and password apps are never written down, nothing it sees is sold, and you can read, fix or delete anything it keeps, or pause it whenever you like.
Figure 5. AffectiveOS arrives inside Braino, in the notch.

You do not install AffectiveOS on its own. It comes inside Braino, which is in private beta on Mac and Chrome right now. We are letting people in a few at a time. Get early access, or read why we are building this.
Replying to an email in under five seconds is the time for Braino to draft the reply; you still read it and press send.
The comparison table describes categories of tools in general, not any single product.
The memory chart is illustrative and is not based on a measurement.

/about.title: About · Affective
/about.pageDescription: Meet Braino. He lives in your Mac's notch and does what you say in the apps you already use. Made by Affective, running on AffectiveOS.
blocks: We believe the future of computing is voice-first. You should be able to just tell your computer what to do.

Itish, who started Affective, grew up on Marvel. Watching Tony Stark talk to Jarvis, and Jarvis simply getting it done, was the computer he always wanted. Not a screen you operate. Something you talk to, that listens, does the work and remembers you.
That picture never left. Affective exists to turn that piece of science fiction into something real, on the Mac you already own.

Affective is a product company. We make things that make life easier, and that you run with your voice. AffectiveOS is the base: it lets a computer see, listen, speak, act and remember. Braino is the first product on it, and it will not be the last. We are already working on what comes next.

We hold ourselves to Apple's standard of craft: nothing ships until it feels obvious and right. We take Anthropic's care with what AI should and should not do on your behalf. And we borrow the best idea from anywhere else. The goal is simple: to be the best at this.
“Tell John I'll be ten minutes late.”
Figure 1. The same message, the old way and ours.

AffectiveOS is the technology. It lets your Mac see your screen, hear you, talk back, use your apps and remember you. Braino is the first product built on it. He lives in your Mac's notch, and you talk to him.

/privacy.title: Affective
/privacy.pageDescription: Meet Braino. He lives in your Mac's notch and does what you say in the apps you already use. Made by Affective, running on AffectiveOS.
blocks: Braino is a browser extension and web service. This policy explains what data we collect, why we collect it, and how you can control it.
We collect the minimum data needed to make Braino work. Here's the full list:
Account data — your email address and a hashed password when you create an account. If you sign in via Google, we receive your name and email from Google.
Conversation history — messages you send to Braino and the responses it gives. These are stored server-side so your history persists across devices.
Page context — when you ask Braino about a page, the text content of that page is sent to our AI model to generate a response. This is processed transiently and not stored long-term.
Audio recordings — if you use the recording feature, audio is transcribed and the resulting text (not the raw audio) is stored in your account.
Usage analytics — anonymous, aggregated data about feature usage (e.g., "20 users used voice mode today"). We do not collect individual click streams.
Browser extension metadata — extension version, browser type. No browsing history, no tabs list, no URL logging beyond what you explicitly share with Braino in a conversation.
Your browsing history or list of visited URLs
Content of pages you visit unless you explicitly ask Braino about them
Financial or payment card details (payments are handled by Stripe)
To provide the service — generating AI responses, maintaining your conversation history, syncing across devices.

To improve the product — understanding which features are used, diagnosing bugs. We may review anonymized conversation samples to improve response quality, but only in aggregate and only with identifying information stripped.
To communicate with you — sending product updates, security notices, and responses to support requests. You can opt out of marketing emails at any time.
To enforce our Terms — detecting abuse, spam, or policy violations.
Braino uses the following third-party processors. Each is bound by their own privacy policies and data processing agreements:
Anthropic / Claude API — AI responses are generated by Claude. Your messages are sent to Anthropic's API. Anthropic does not use API data to train models by default. See anthropic.com/legal/privacy.
Supabase — database, authentication, and storage hosting. Data is stored in secure, encrypted databases.
Stripe — payment processing for Pro subscriptions. We never see or store your card number.
Fish Audio — text-to-speech generation for Braino's voice. Text snippets are sent to Fish Audio's API.
We do not sell your data to advertisers or data brokers. Ever.

We keep your conversation history for as long as your account is active. If you delete your account, all personal data is permanently deleted within 30 days. You can request deletion of specific conversations from your account settings at any time.
Anonymous, aggregated analytics data may be retained indefinitely because it cannot be linked back to you.
Depending on where you live, you may have the right to:
Access — request a copy of all personal data we hold about you.
Correction — request correction of inaccurate data.
Deletion — request that we delete your account and all associated data.
Portability — request your conversation history in a machine-readable format.
Objection — object to processing of your data for certain purposes.
To exercise any of these rights, email us at talk2braino@gmail.com. We'll respond within 30 days.
Braino is not directed at children under 13. We do not knowingly collect personal data from children. If we discover we have collected data from a child under 13, we will delete it promptly.

We use industry-standard encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest. Access to user data is restricted to engineers who require it for their work, and all access is logged. We conduct regular security reviews.
No system is perfectly secure. If you discover a vulnerability, please report it responsibly to talk2braino@gmail.com.
The Braino website uses session cookies for authentication. We use no third-party tracking cookies. We do not run retargeting ads.
The browser extension does not set or read cookies from third-party websites.

If we make material changes to how we handle your data, we'll notify you via email and update the "Last updated" date at the top of this page. Continued use of the service after changes constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.
Questions about privacy? Email talk2braino@gmail.com. We're a small team and we read every email.
